nodes.label: Gateway-Mode Verification Substitution (deferred M0->M1->M2)
nodes.rationale: Live PID-bound gateway sessions on the default and n8nian profiles at verification time made running the literal `hermes gateway run` procedure risky (could disrupt a real Discord session), so the already-running-loop branch was exercised directly via discover_plugins()/dispatch() instead; substitution carried forward across M0, M1, and M2, deferred again to M3.

nodes.label: HDPRuntime.close() shutdown race bug
nodes.rationale: loop.call_soon_threadsafe(loop.stop) could abort transport.start() mid-flight, leaking a bound socket. Fixed via a threading.Event-based poll (_serve_until_close_requested) so start() always completes before a close request is checked; verified via 10 repeated start/stop cycles with no fd/thread growth.

nodes.label: Intermittent KeyError: 'HERMES_HOME' bug
nodes.rationale: Suspected race with Hermes's own os.environ mutation in the host process; not root-caused. Mitigated (not fixed) by retrying _write_bridge_addr() up to 3 times on KeyError during start(), and EmbeddedServer.close() swallowing KeyError/OSError on best-effort bridge.addr cleanup since a stale bridge.addr is harmless.

nodes.label: Task 19 (daemon autostart) cut decision
nodes.rationale: Pre-declared optional cut line in the plan; cut due to repeated external session-limit interruptions across Tasks 3, 7, 10, 12, 15. Cost if wrong is low (cheap, additive future implementation). Shipped MVP answer: run `hdp-bridge serve` manually in a foreground terminal.

nodes.label: Deviation: two SQLite connections in daemon.py, not one
nodes.rationale: Registry.__init__ opens its own connection internally rather than accepting a shared one, so _serve_claimed opens a second independent connection for NodeConnection/credentials.py/pairing.py. Safe because WAL mode makes committed writes visible across connections, the daemon is single-threaded/single-writer, and the one place cross-connection ordering matters (_handle_hello's pairing path) is written in the safe order deliberately.
nodes.norm_label: deviation: two sqlite connections in daemon.py, not one

nodes.label: Deviation: POST /hdp/v0/pair remains absent from HTTP surface
nodes.rationale: Pairing implemented entirely through the WebSocket handshake's pair:-prefixed credential; a second HTTP round trip before the upgrade would need its own auth story for no benefit since the pairing code is already the one-time secret.
nodes.norm_label: deviation: post /hdp/v0/pair remains absent from http surface

nodes.label: Deviation: /hdp pair and /hdp devices revoke are CLI-only (finding I1)
nodes.rationale: In gateway mode /hdp runs inside the always-running plugin process, turning the plan's sanctioned short-lived-CLI exception into an in-process one; /hdp keeps read-only verbs and points mutating verbs to hermes hdp CLI, also keeping plaintext pairing codes out of gateway chat transcripts.

nodes.label: HDP Transport Rules (WS ping/pong, no client-IP trust, bind guard)
nodes.rationale: Exist because the eventual deployment is a public hostname behind a tunnel, not a bare LAN; retrofitting after M1 ships would mean changing a shipped protocol, so they land now even though the tunnel itself is out of MVP scope.

nodes.label: Pending-table-entry-removed-before-cancel-send ordering rule
nodes.rationale: Reversing the order (sending cancel before removing the pending-table entry) leaks an entry whenever the send itself fails.

nodes.label: Binary Payload Rule (metadata in JSON, binary by content ID, no base64-in-envelope)
nodes.rationale: Roughly twenty lines of cost now, versus a protocol break the first time something needs to send a screenshot.

nodes.label: device.status@1 is deliberately not what device_status_get calls
nodes.rationale: device_status_get reports bridge-side registry state (runtime.transport.list_devices()) and does not invoke any capability over the wire; device.status@1 exists so the capability itself is exercised end to end by the conformance suite, independent of the tool sharing its name. Confirmed explicitly during M1 planning; rewiring device_status_get through engine.invoke() was out of scope for M1.
nodes.norm_label: device.status@1 is deliberately not what device_status_get calls

nodes.label: notifications.send@1 input schema byte-identical to schemas.py NOTIFICATIONS_SEND (minus device field)
nodes.rationale: Routing which device to target is a plugin/tool-level concern; the node never sees it since corr/dispatch already resolved a specific connection by the time invoke reaches the node.
nodes.norm_label: notifications.send@1 input schema byte-identical to schemas.py notifications_send (minus device field)
